notes: Sourced from live Wikipedia rosters (15th Maharashtra Assembly, List of members of the Maharashtra Legislative Council, 15th Gujarat Assembly, 8th Goa Assembly), fetched 2026-09-25. Bypoll/defection/death replacements already reflected by those pages as of fetch time (e.g. MH: Sunetra Pawar replaced Ajit Pawar in Baramati since 2026-05-04 following his death 2026-01-28; Akshay Kardile replaced Shivaji Kardile in Rahuri, elected 2026 following his death 2025-10-17; GJ: 8 seats changed hands via death/resignation bypolls or defection between 2024-2025; GA: 8 MLAs switched from INC to BJP on 2022-09-14, shown here under their current party). Maharashtra Legislative Council: 73 of 78 seats have a confirmed current holder from the Wikipedia roster (22 Local Authorities, 7 Graduates, 7 Teachers, 30 MLA-elected, 7 of 12 Governor-nominated); the remaining 5 nominated seats are vacant, marked here with confidence 'medium' (see `verification` block: one of these, st-mh-pos-mlc-nom-8, was corrected from a stale 2000-2002 historical record to vacant on 2026-09-25). Election dates for non-bypoll MLAs use each state's principal poll date, not per-phase polling-day granularity for multi-phase elections. Council seat labels use category (Local Authorities/Graduates/Teachers/MLA-elected/Nominated) per SCHEMA.md guidance rather than the historical Wikipedia constituency name (which has been renamed over decades, e.g. 'Thane-Palghar LA' -> 'Thane LA').

verification.method: 1) Structural: validated JSON parses, ID-format (lowercase kebab, `st-(mh|gj|ga)-pos-mla-*` / `st-mh-pos-mlc-*`), 0 duplicate position ids, per-house counts (MH Assembly 288, MH Council 78, GJ Assembly 182, GA Assembly 40 = 588 total), required-field presence on all 588 positions (1 gap found: st-mh-pos-mlc-nom-8 holder missing `since` -- moot, see corrections). 2) Confirmed each house is the sitting one from the latest general election (15th Maharashtra Assembly, Nov 2024; 15th Gujarat Assembly, Dec 2022; 8th Goa Assembly, 2022) via the same Wikipedia articles already cited as sources. 3) By-election/death/resignation/disqualification search for 2025-2026 across all 4 houses: raw-parsed (curl + Wikipedia parse API wikitext, not WebFetch prose summarization, to avoid summarizer hallucination) `15th_Maharashtra_Assembly`, `15th_Gujarat_Assembly`, `8th_Goa_Assembly`, and `List_of_members_of_the_Maharashtra_Legislative_Council`, grepping for Resigned/Died/Disqualified/Elected-on/By-election patterns dated 2024-2026. 4) Recomputed party-wise `stats` on all 4 legislature entities directly from `positions` (Counter over holder.party / vacant). 5) Spot-checked 30 randomly sampled (seed=42) non-vacant positions' name+party+constituency against a fresh raw wikitext parse of the same Wikipedia articles (independent re-parse, not just re-reading the file); during that pass also investigated every current Governor-nominated MLC against the Council page's `16-Oct-2024` nominee cohort specifically. Resource constraints: WebSearch was already at its 200/200 session-wide cap before this task started (shared across concurrent sibling agents), so all checks used curl/WebFetch against Wikipedia rather than a live news search -- undetected 2025-2026 changes not yet reflected on Wikipedia (or reported only in press not yet in these articles) would not surface. One WebFetch summarization was caught producing wrong output (claimed Sangli MLA was 'Vishal Patil' and Visavadar was 'BJP'; both are wrong -- raw wikitext confirms Sudhir Gadgil and AAP's Gopal Italia respectively, matching the file) and was not used for anything beyond a first pass.
